name: CompLex 2.0 / SemEval 2021 Task 1

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.scope: Dataset text and numeric ratings; excludes third-party article/reading-material full texts.

lexical_complexity.instruction: Predict the lexical complexity of the target word or expression in its English sentence. Scores range from 0 (least complex) to 1 (most complex).
lexical_complexity.field_description: sentence: Original English sentence providing context.; target_token: Word or multiword expression to assess.; corpus: Source domain: bible, biomed or europarl.; expression_type: single for a single word, multi for a multiword expression.

field_descriptions.target_token: Word or multiword expression to assess.
field_descriptions.corpus: Source domain: bible, biomed or europarl.
field_descriptions.expression_type: single for a single word, multi for a multiword expression.

text_policy: Original selected text and capitalization preserved byte-for-byte after UTF-8/CSV decoding; grouping uses a separate whitespace-normalized casefolded hash. No spelling correction, truncation, label imputation, or score transformation.
grouping_rule: Connected components of casefolded target tokens and whitespace-normalized casefolded sentences, spanning both expression types. Group IDs do not alter official splits.
split_policy: Official train retained; official trial mapped to validation; labelled test retained as test. Connected groups or exact inputs crossing official partitions are flagged. For a strict grouped evaluation, assign entire groups jointly before fitting; never use row order as a feature.
source_citation: Shardlow et al. (2021), SemEval-2021 Task 1: Lexical Complexity Prediction, https://aclanthology.org/2021.semeval-1.1/
quality_findings: Sentence-level deduplication would discard distinct lexical targets and is not performed.
TSV is parsed without CSV quote handling: quotation marks in sentences are literal source text.
Trial uses column subcorpus; train/test use corpus. Both are mapped to input.corpus without changing their values.
Original file order can reflect complexity; source row and ID are provenance only.
Crowd-averaged Likert ratings are continuous on the published 0-1 scale.

checks: All retained labels finite and within documented rating scale
Every retained input and label compared with its original decoded CSV/TSV row
Every source row accounted for; invalid/missing labels never imputed
Explicit input allowlists exclude source IDs, other scores, bins, demographics and article full texts
Official splits retained; cross-split identical inputs and connected groups counted and flagged
Source version, downloaded bytes and SHA256 recorded

deduplication_rule: Same task, normalized input, normalized label AND official split; preserve all source_refs. Across-split copies retained and flagged, same-input dependencies unioned. Different labels retained.
sample_id_rule: sha256([task_id,input_hash,label,split]) first 24 hex; official split included to preserve split occurrences.
